long_biography.plain_text:
At Sydney property developer Dyldam, Fayad-Lee Fayad moved from building sites into senior management, spending four years as chief operating officer before becoming chief executive. He continued making daily site rounds, using knowledge gained as a leading hand to test construction decisions with experienced tradespeople.

Ellerson Property adopted a development-agency model when Fayad and his brother launched it in 2020. Rather than owning project sites itself, the business coordinates planning, design, construction, sales and ongoing management for family-owned land and external clients. Fayad concentrates on architecture and construction, while Remon Fayad handles planning and acquisitions.

uncertainties.detail: The upstream record's Fayad-Lee Fayad form is confirmed by the Australian Business Register and Federal Court material. Business interviews and the existing LinkedIn account use Fayad Fayad or Fayad S. Fayad, but their Ellerson, Dyldam, Western Sydney, father and brother details converge on the same person. The S initial is not expanded by a reliable source, so middle_names remains blank.

Dyldam was an established maternal-family business before Fayad joined; his father held a senior role, Fayad succeeded into the chief-executive position, and later reporting identifies him as an Ellerson owner while Ellerson managed family-owned sites. These positive premises support a medium-confidence family transfer. No source reviewed states that shares were inherited or identifies the legal transfer instrument, so the dossier does not use Inherited or Inherited and expanded.

The dossier does not infer wealth merely from the title property developer. It relies on direct ownership of Ellerson, an active sole-trader business registration, sustained control of the family development platform and Federal Court interim material identifying an apparent ultimate economic interest in a property through intermediary companies. Exact current net worth, project-by-project ownership and the value of individual stakes are not public, so Real Estate creation is a medium-confidence materiality inference rather than a precise asset schedule.

Fayad's historical operator role is direct and extensive, but Federal Court material records his July 2025 bankruptcy. An active ABN, a live company domain and an older LinkedIn role do not establish which assets remain personally controlled after that event. Primary industry therefore uses the disclosed Real Estate origin-sector fallback, while wealth relationship remains Unknown; Operator is preserved as the strongest historical alternative but is not carried forward as current.

The published biographies retain the durable professional story and family-business context. They omit vessel material, development-pipeline figures, legal allegations, judgments and debt totals because those facts are unnecessary to explain Fayad's defining work and would date the profile. The 2025 bankruptcy is retained in classification metadata because it materially limits current-industry and relationship claims.

The upstream record supplies Australian nationality and a 7 June 1982 birth date, but the strongest public sources reviewed do not independently establish a birthplace, secondary nationality or expanded middle name. Lebanese family heritage is not treated as proof of Lebanese nationality. No personal-detail proposal is made for those fields.

The existing LinkedIn URL is identity-secure through Ellerson, Western Sydney, education and company-domain links. The existing Instagram handle was not duplicated or changed. Ellerson's official domain is proposed as a Company Website because strong sources establish Fayad as its co-founder and owner. No identity-secure Personal Website, Facebook, X, YouTube or TikTok account was established.

The mandatory exact Forbes profile and exact-name searches were performed first after inventory. No dedicated profile for Fayad-Lee Fayad or the Australian Ellerson co-founder was found; Forbes results for Andrew Fayad concern an unrelated e-learning executive. No Forbes social link is proposed.

Property developer and Residential development answer separate useful questions: Fayad's defining practiced occupation and the narrower high-rise residential sector in which he exercised sustained control. Both are marked former but defining because the evidence securely establishes a long-term public identity but does not establish current operating control after bankruptcy. No company tag is invented for Ellerson or Dyldam.
